 Judgment

This miscellaneous first appeal is filed under Section 173(1) of Motor Vehicles Act (for short 'the MV Act') by the claimants seeking enhancement of the compensation granted by the Tribunal for the death of one Sanjeev Kate in a motor vehicle accident dated 26.04.2013.
2. For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to by their rank before the Tribunal.
3. It is the case of the petitioners that they are the parents of the deceased Sanjeev Kate.
On 24.06.2013 at about 6-30 p.m., he was proceeding as a pillion rider on motorcycle bearing registration No.MH-13/AY-3175.
It was ridden by Mallikarjun Hattaraki.

Near Nandur village on Vijayapura- Mangalweda road, a Tempo bearing registration No.MH-12/FC-6598 (hereinafter referred as "the offending vehicle") came in a high speed, in a rash or negligent manner and dashed against the motorcycle.
In the said accident, Sanjeev Kate sustained grievous inquires and died.
He was an agriculturist.
The deceased was earning Rs.15,000/- p.m.
The petitioners were dependent on him.
As the owner and insurer, the respondents are liable to pay the compensation.
4. Before the Tribunal, though duly served, respondent No.1 remained ex parte.
5. Respondent No.2 appeared and filed written statement denying the age, occupation, income of the deceased.
The driver of the offending vehicle was not holding a valid driving licence.
Its liability is subject to the terms and conditions of the policy.
6. Based on the pleadings, the Tribunal has framed necessary issues.
7. On behalf of the petitioners, petitioner No.1 is examined as P.W.1 and relied upon documentary evidence.

8. Respondent No.2 got marked Exs.R.1 & 2.
9.
Vide the impugned judgment and award, the Tribunal has partly allowed the petition granting compensation in sum of Rs.8,36,000/- with interest at 9% per annum as detailed below :

 10. Respondents have not challenged the impugned judgment and award.
11. During course of arguments, learned counsel for the appellant submitted that the income of the deceased ought to have been taken at Rs.15,000/- p.m.
While granting loss of dependency, loss of future prospects is not taken into consideration.
The compensation grated under other heads also requires enhancement.
12. On the other hand, learned counsel for respondent No.2 supported the impugned judgment and award and prays to dismiss the appeal.

13. Heard arguments and perused the records.
14.
Through the testimony of P.W.1, petitioners have proved that deceased died in a motor vehicle accident dated 26.04.2013.
After detailed investigation, the concerned police have filed chargesheet against the driver of the offending vehicle.

Admittedly,
as on the date of accident, the offending vehicle was covered by a valid policy.

Considering the oral and documentary evidence placed on record, the Tribunal has rightly held that the accident occurred due to the rash or negligent driving of the offending vehicle by its driver and as the insurer, respondent No.2 is liable to indemnify the owner i.e., respondent No.1.
15.

Therefore, the only question that is to be decided is whether the quantum of compensation granted by the Tribunal is just and reasonable under the following heads:

sentences.text: Loss of dependency:- The petitioners claimed that the deceased was aged 20 years.
However based on the documents, the Tribunal has correctly taken the age of the deceased as 25 years and appropriate multiplier 18.
The petitioners have not produced any documents to prove that the deceased was earning Rs.15,000/- p.m.
Since the accident is of the year 2013, the Tribunal has justified in considering the income of the deceased on notional basis at Rs.7,000/- p.m.

However,
the Tribunal has not considered loss of future prospects.

Since the deceased was aged less than 40 years, as per Magma General Insurance Company Limited Vs. Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram And Others1 (Magma's case), 40% is required to be added towards loss of future prospects.

entities.text: Magma General Insurance Company Limited Vs. Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram And Others1 (Magma's case)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 40% of Rs.7,000/- comes to Rs.2,800/- and therefore, the income of the deceased is required to be take at Rs.9,800/- p.m.
Since the deceased was a bachelor, 50% is required to be deducted towards the personal and living expenses of the deceased.
With these components, the loss of dependency comes to Rs.9,800 x 12 x 18 x 50% = Rs.10,58,400/ as against Rs.7,56,000/- granted by the Tribunal.
17. Loss of consortium:-
The Tribunal has granted compensation in a sum of Rs.50,000/- under the head loss of love and affection.

As per National Insurance Company Limited V. Pranay Sethi and others2 (Pranay Sethi's case), under the head loss of consortium, the wife, parents and children of the deceased are entitled for compensation in a sum of Rs.40,000/- each.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, petitioners are entitled (2018) 18 SCC 130 for Rs.40,000/- each under this head.
When compensation is granted under the head loss of consortium, no separate compensation is required to be granted under the head loss of love and affection.
Therefore, Rs.50,000/- granted under the head loss of love and affection is disallowed.

18. Loss to estate and Funeral expenses:-
The Tribunal has granted compensation in a sum of Rs.10,000/- each under the head loss to estate, funeral and transportation expenses.

When major compensation is granted under the head loss of dependency, as per Pranay Sethi's case referred to supra under the conventional head of loss to estate and funeral expenses (which includes transportation charges), a sum of Rs.15,000/- each is required to be granted.

Therefore, compensation under the heads loss to estate and funeral expenses is enhanced to (2017) 16 SCC 680 Rs.15,000/- each & separate compensation in a sum of Rs.10,000/- granted under the head transportation of dead body is disallowed.

19. Thus, in all the petitioners are entitled for compensation in a sum of Rs.11,68,400/- together with interest at 6% p.a., as against Rs.8,36,000/- granted by the Tribunal as detailed below:

4. Funeral Rs.10,000/- Rs.15,000/-

Of course as the insurer of the offending vehicle, respondent No.2 is liable to pay the enhanced compensation with interest.

Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER (i) The Appeal is allowed in part.

(ii) The appellants/petitioners are entitled for compensation in a sum of Rs.11,68,400/- together with interest at 6% p.a. on the enhanced compensation as against Rs.8,36,000/- granted by the Tribunal.
(iii) Respondent No.2/Insurance company shall deposit the compensation amount within a period of six weeks from the date of this order together with interest.
